doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: Boys chased out of the District by police
summary: Young men were run out of the Storyville district with a strap; Percy recalls being too busy with music for girls.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: All I can tell you during the district, when we young men like that go around there, the police will take a strap. When I'm 68 years old at present, and I just called almost the last part of the district. I wouldn't tell you a lie that I played in the district, but I know about it. And we go around there, they just take, with being boys, they take this strap and they beat you on your backside and chase you out. They know what you do is just scare you. And we respect men to them days, you understand? It's not any going person. Yeah. In case you'll just run us away from around there. Yeah, you have to be a man to go over there. Yeah.

When I went over there, ooh, I just went over to the base and looked at all them pretty people past. I said, Jesus Christ, I want to be 21 years old. But I didn't call it. You know what I mean? Mary said, oh, the Lord said, oh, he's a man now. Yeah, he's a boy. Oh, Jesus Christ. I said, I want to go by his daddy and lose some to all the first jobs and playing. I was a young fellow there too, you know. But otherwise, you know, I never let no girls then know. I was busy with music. I didn't like them. And then girls that come to my house and my sister lost saved with Jim. I said, oh, I'm not a girl. I said, I don't put no girls. That's right. I had one girl. He said, her name was quite true. And I love that girl, understand? But I would never tell them about the mothers. They would be flashing. I said, oh, Lord. I like one.
